groups.name: Prof. Derek Sullivan
groups.title: Head of Division · Principal Investigator
groups.bio: My research has covered many aspects of the biology of the human pathogenic yeasts Candida albicans and Candida dubliniensis. Most recently, our research has investigated the role of the greatly expanded TLO gene family in pathogenesis and in responses to antifungal drugs.

members.name: Abed Alkarem Abu Al Haija
members.degree: PhD in Molecular Biology and Genetics
members.bio: Gene regulation in the fungal pathogen Candida albicans. Studying the TLO gene family, which encodes subunits of the Mediator complex that controls gene expression, and the RNA interference (RNAi) system, to understand how they shape gene expression, stress adaptation and virulence.
members.profile:
I study how cells control which genes are switched on, and how families of related genes share out that job. I have followed this question across three kingdoms of life: plants during my MSc, mouse embryonic stem cells during my PhD, and now the fungal pathogen Candida albicans.

groups.name: Prof. Gary Moran
groups.title: Professor in Microbiology · Principal Investigator
groups.bio: I run the Oral Microbiome research group in the School of Dental Science. My research focuses on the pathogenicity of oral microorganisms, including the fungal pathogen Candida albicans and the oral bacterium Fusobacterium nucleatum. Our research combines molecular genetics, genomics and transcriptomics, and we also carry out metagenomics of the oral microbiome to better understand oral disease.

members.name: Emma Moore
members.bio: Within-host genomic diversity of vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium (VREfm) in hospitalised patients, dogs and the environment. Using whole-genome sequencing and a One Health approach, with a focus on vanA-carrying plasmids.

management.name: Dr Ajith Kumar Selvaraj
management.role: Experimental Officer and Research Laboratory Manager
management.bio: My research focuses on the role of the oral microbiome in the progression of oral squamous cell carcinoma (oral cancer).

former.name: Prof. David Coleman
former.role: Professor of Oral and Applied Microbiology (retired) · FTCD, MRIA, FRCPath
former.bio: David Coleman joined the School of Dental Science in 1989 and led the lab's microbiology research for more than three decades, serving as Head of the Division of Oral Biosciences. He co-discovered Candida dubliniensis in 1995, pioneered automated decontamination of dental unit waterlines, and built a long-running programme on the genomics and antibiotic resistance of MRSA and other hospital pathogens. He has published more than 240 peer-reviewed papers and received the Royal Irish Academy Silver Medal for Microbiology.
